User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the VoltaConnect platform with specific roles and associated details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The email address of the user.

role.description: The role of the user within the system (Super Admin, Operator, End User).

associatedStationId.description: Reference to the Station associated with an Operator. (Relationship: Station 1:N User)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

Station.title: Station
Station.description: Represents an EV charging station managed by the platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Station entity.

name.description: The name of the charging station.

location.description: Geographical location details of the station.

status.description: Current operational status of the station (active/offline).

operatorId.description: Reference to the Operator managing this station. (Relationship: User 1:N Station)

totalPower.description: Total power capacity of the station in kW.

chargerCount.description: Number of individual chargers available at this station.

Charger.title: Charger
Charger.description: Represents an individual EV charger unit within a station.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Charger entity.

stationId.description: Reference to the Station this charger belongs to. (Relationship: Station 1:N Charger)

currentUsage.description: Current power usage of the charger in kW.

status.description: Current operational status of the charger (available, occupied, out_of_service).

ratePerKwh.description: Charging rate per kilowatt-hour for this charger.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Records details of a completed EV charging session.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

userId.description: Reference to the End User who initiated the transaction. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction)

stationId.description: Reference to the Station where the transaction occurred. (Relationship: Station 1:N Transaction)

duration.description: Duration of the charging session in minutes.

cost.description: Total cost of the charging session.

energyDelivered.description: Total energy delivered during the session in kWh.

timestamp.description: Date and time when the transaction was recorded.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents a user's reservation for a charging slot at a specific station.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

userId.description: Reference to the End User who made this booking. (Relationship: User 1:N Booking)

stationId.description: Reference to the Station where the booking is made. (Relationship: Station 1:N Booking)

bookingDate.description: The date of the booking in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).

bookingTime.description: The time of the booking in 24-hour format (HH:mm).

status.description: The current status of the booking (pending, confirmed, rejected).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the booking request was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the booking status was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. The primary goal is Authorization Independence, meaning security rules avoid hierarchical dependencies and `get()` calls for authorization decisions on the target resource. This is achieved through strategic denormalization and structural segregation.

1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** This collection stores core user data like email and creation timestamp. The 'role' and 'associatedStationId' fields for Operators are stored here. For security rules, `request.auth.uid` will fetch its own user document to determine its role and associated station, which is considered an acceptable 'self-context' `get()` and does not violate the Authorization Independence mandate which primarily targets `get()` calls on *other* documents to authorize access to the *target resource*.

2.  **Stations (`/stations/{stationId}`):** Stations are stored in a top-level collection. Crucially, each `Station` document includes the `operatorId` of the user responsible for managing it. This denormalization ensures that an operator's access to manage a station can be verified by simply checking `request.auth.uid == resource.data.operatorId`, without needing to `get()` the operator's user profile or any other related document for authorization.

3.  **Chargers (`/stations/{stationId}/chargers/{chargerId}`):** Chargers are placed in a subcollection under their respective stations. To maintain Authorization Independence for chargers, each `Charger` document will also denormalize the `operatorId` from its parent `Station`. This allows operator-specific rules for chargers to directly check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.operatorId`, preventing a `get()` call to the parent `Station` for authorization. This also supports efficient collection group queries for operators listing *all* their chargers across stations.

4.  **Transactions (`/users/{userId}/transactions/{transactionId}`):** Transactions are stored as a subcollection under the `users` collection. This path-based ownership provides inherent security, where users can only access their own transactions (i.e., `request.auth.uid == userId`). The `stationId` is also included directly in the document, but for read-only informational purposes, not for access control of the transaction itself.

5.  **Bookings (`/bookings/{bookingId}`):** Bookings are critical for slot validation and role-based workflows. They are placed in a root-level collection for several reasons:
    *   **QAPs (Queryable Access Patterns):** This structure supports all required queries efficiently:
        *   **User's 'My Bookings':** A simple query `bookings.where('userId', '==', request.auth.uid)` is performant.
        *   **Operator's Bookings:** A query `bookings.where('operatorId', '==', request.auth.uid)` is performant. This requires `operatorId` to be denormalized into the `Booking` document.
        *   **Availability Check:** The core requirement of querying for `station_id`, `booking_date`, `booking_time`, and `status in ['confirmed', 'pending']` is highly efficient with a top-level collection and the specified composite index. No `get()` calls are needed for this client-side validation query.
    *   **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** Each `Booking` document explicitly includes `userId` (the user who made the booking), `stationId` (the station being booked), and `operatorId` (the ID of the station's assigned operator). This extensive denormalization means that all authorization rules (e.g., user can cancel their booking, operator can approve/reject a booking for their station) can be evaluated solely based on the `resource.data` of the booking document itself, comparing `request.auth.uid` directly against `userId` or `operatorId`. This eliminates `get()` calls to `User` or `Station` documents for authorization of the booking resource, fulfilling Mandate A.

This structure ensures clear authorization intent, supports robust security rules, and allows for efficient queries required by both end-users and operators, while strictly adhering to the principle of Authorization Independence.
